Quick thought / options for Straintline to consider (trying to keep to your timeline):
1) Redwood standard — Governing law: California; venue: courts in San Francisco; arbitration clause for monetary claims (AAA), but express carve for injunctive relief (either party may seek provisional relief in any court). This is our most straightforward path.
2) Hybrid compromise — Governing law: Delaware (as you request) *but* explicit language preserving the right to seek injunctive relief in any court (so remedies aren't limited to arbitration); arbitration for monetary claims administered by AAA in San Francisco. Requires a short legal concession on our side but keeps emergency relief clear.
3) Customer-preferred forum — Accept Delaware law and JAMS/AAA in New York for arbitration, but Redwood asks for a narrow IP/injunction exception limited to preservation and short-term provisional relief, after which claims go to arbitration. This is our heaviest concession and would need legal sign-off.

Laura, can you prioritize and give a redline for option 2 (hybrid) so I can send to Amelia as Redwood's counter-proposal? Karthik — flag impact to sales timeline if we have to escalate.

Thanks —
S

Stephanie —

Thanks for the ping. I reviewed Straintline's PDF and propose we lead with option 2 (hybrid compromise) but with tightened language to protect Redwood's operational footprint. Key reasons: preserves our ability to enforce urgent relief quickly while conceding governing law to their preference in contract formation.

Suggested clause (redline-ready):
"Governing Law and Injunctive Relief. This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to conflict of law rules. Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may seek provisional, interim or injunctive relief from any court of competent jurisdiction to protect its intellectual property, confidential information, or other rights or property, without first submitting the dispute to arbitration. The parties agree that any final determination of non‑monetary claims shall be governed by the court as set forth herein, and monetary claims shall be resolved by binding arbitration as provided below."

Arbitration (money-only):
"All disputes seeking monetary damages shall be submitted to binding arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association in San Francisco, California, under the AAA rules then in effect. Each party reserves the right to seek provisional remedies in any court as needed to preserve the status quo or protect proprietary assets prior to arbitration."

Operational notes:
- We should limit injunctive relief carve to preservation and emergency enforcement, not to create a parallel forum for all merits disputes.
- If Straintline insists on JAMS/NY or a Delaware seat, ask for a reciprocal concession on audit/audit-venue or extended SLAs.

I'll attach a short .docx with the redline text. If you want, I can convert to tracked changes and send directly to Amelia.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
